   806	\begin{definition}[Expanded state]
   807		\label{def:expanded-state}
   808		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.SixReg, MIPStarRE.QPBT.ProjectiveSetting.psiHat}
   809		\leanok
   810		\uses{lem:projective-strategy-setup, def:EPR}
   811		Recall that $M = 2^m$. Introduce registers $\mathsf{A}', \mathsf{A}'',
   812		\mathsf{B}', \mathsf{B}''$, each with Hilbert space isomorphic to
   813		$(\C^q)^{\ot M}$, and define the state
   814		\begin{equation}\label{eq:def-psihat}
   815			\ket{\hat{\psi}}_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'\mathsf{A}''\mathsf{B}\mathsf{B}'\mathsf{B}''}
   816			\,=\, (\ket{\psi})_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{B}}
   817			\ot \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}_{\mathsf{A}'\mathsf{A}''}
   818			\ot \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}_{\mathsf{B}'\mathsf{B}''}\,,
   819		\end{equation}
   820		where $\ket{\psi}$ is the extended strategy state of the strategy
   821		under analysis (Lemma~\ref{lem:projective-strategy-setup} and the
   822		convention following it) and
   823		$\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}$ is the maximally entangled state on
   824		$\C^q \ot \C^q$ (Definition~\ref{def:EPR}). For the remainder of this
   825		chapter, as well as in Chapters~\ref{chap:qpbt-combining}
   826		and~\ref{chap:qpbt-extraction}, all approximations $\approx$ and
   827		$\simeq$ are evaluated with respect to the state $\ket{\hat{\psi}}$,
   828		unless stated otherwise.
   829	\end{definition}
   830	
   831	\begin{definition}[Expanded observables]
   832		\label{def:expanded-observables}
   833		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.ProjectiveSetting.expObs}
   834		\leanok
   835		\uses{def:strategy-observables, def:expanded-state, lem:twisted-commutation}
   836		For all $W \in \{X,Z\}$, $r \in \F_q$, and $u \in \F_q^m$, define the
   837		observable
   838		\begin{equation}\label{eq:lc-23}
   839			\hat{W}^r(u) \,=\, W^r(u) \ot \tau^W(r \cdot \mathrm{ind}_m(u))\,,
   840		\end{equation}
   841		where $W^r(u)$ is the strategy observable of~\eqref{eq:qld-strat-obs}
   842		and $\tau^W(r \cdot \mathrm{ind}_m(u))$ is the generalized Pauli
   843		observable acting on $(\C^q)^{\ot M}$, introduced in
   844		Chapter~\ref{chap:qpbt-algebra}
   845		(see Lemma~\ref{lem:twisted-commutation}). As a product
   846		of two observables with eigenvalues $\pm 1$ acting on disjoint
   847		registers, $\hat{W}^r(u)$ is itself an observable with eigenvalues
   848		$\pm 1$. If $W^r(u)$ is viewed as acting on register $\mathsf{A}$, then
   849		$\hat{W}^r(u)$ is viewed as acting on registers
   850		$\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'$, with the $\tau^W$ factor acting on
   851		$\mathsf{A}'$. The registers are generally indicated by subscripts, as
   852		in $(\hat{W}^r(u))_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'}$ or
   853		$(\hat{W}^r(u))_{\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''}$, the latter having the
   854		strategy factor on $\mathsf{B}$ and the Pauli factor on
   855		$\mathsf{A}''$.
   856	\end{definition}
   857	
   858	\begin{definition}[Expanded point measurements]
   859		\label{def:expanded-point-measurement}
   860		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.ProjectiveSetting.expPointOp}
   861		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.ProjectiveSetting.tauPointProj}
   862		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.ProjectiveSetting.pointMeasExp}
   863		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.ProjectiveSetting.expPointOp_eq_convolution}
   864		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.ProjectiveSetting.pointMeasExp_isProjective}

   868		\[
   869			\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a \,=\, \E_{r \in \F_q} (-1)^{\tr(ar)} \, \hat{W}^r(u)\,,
   870		\]

   872		\begin{equation}\label{eq:qld-point-obs-def}
   873			\tau^{W,u}_a \,=\, \tau^W_{[g_\cdot(u) = a]}
   874			\,=\, \sum_{h \in \F_q^{M} \colon h \cdot \mathrm{ind}_m(u) = a} \tau^W_h\,,

   881		generalized Pauli observables

   883		averaging over $r$, gives the equivalent convolution form

    17	\section{At a glance}
    18	
    19	\begin{itemize}
    20	  \item \textbf{Difficulty.} Low.  The paper's global polynomial shorthand
    21	  couples two constants in a way that excludes a square-root function used
    22	  explicitly later in the same paper.
    23	  \item \textbf{Estimated weight.} The formal correction is one predicate with
    24	  separate prefactor and exponent witnesses; no theorem statement changes.
    25	  \item \textbf{Mathlib/project split.} The obstruction is elementary real
    26	  analysis.  Mathlib's real-power API will discharge concrete downstream
    27	  witnesses, while the corrected convention is project-local.
    28	  \item \textbf{Key Mathlib inputs.} The downstream witnesses use the
    29	  \path{Real.rpow} API.  The obstruction here is the elementary fact that no
    30	  constant $C>0$ can bound $\sqrt{x}$ by $C x^C$ for every $x>0$.
    31	\end{itemize}
    32	
    33	\section{Key theorem forms}
    34	
    35	The paper's shorthand asks for one universal constant $C>0$ such that
    36	\[
    37	  f(x) \leq Cx^C \qquad (x>0).
    38	\]
    39	The formal one-parameter convention instead asks for constants $A\geq1$ and
    40	$r>0$ such that
    41	\[
    42	  0\leq f(x)\leq Ax^r \qquad (x\geq0).
    43	\]
    44	This form includes $f(x)=\sqrt{x}$ by taking $A=1$ and $r=1/2$.
    45	
    46	\section{The source convention}
    47	
    48	The asymptotic conventions of \cite[lines~23--29]{Ji2020MIPStar} define
    49	$f(x)=\operatorname{poly}(x)$ using the same constant as prefactor and
    50	exponent.  Later, the Pauli basis analysis explicitly obtains
    51	$\delta_{\mathrm{acom}}(\eps)=\sqrt{\eps}$ and
    52	$\delta_{\mathrm{Line}}(\eps)=\sqrt{\eps}$ at lines~508--520 and 649--676 of
    53	the chapter-14 source mirror.\footnote{The corresponding files are
    54	\path{references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex} and
    55	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex}.  The
    56	formal correction is tracked in
    57	\href{https://github.com/Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A/issues/16}{GitHub issue \#16}
    58	and descends from \localissue{0002}.}
    59	
    60	The coupled-constant inequality cannot hold for $f(x)=\sqrt{x}$.  At $x=1$ it
    61	would imply $C\geq1$.  For such a constant,
    62	\[
    63	  \frac{\sqrt{x}}{Cx^C}=C^{-1}x^{1/2-C}
    64	\]
    65	is unbounded as $x$ decreases to zero, contradicting the proposed inequality
    66	on all positive inputs.
    67	
    68	\section{Comparison with the blueprint and formalization}
    69	
    70	The blueprint records only the paper's local assertions that the relevant
    71	errors are polynomial in $\eps$; those assertions include the displayed
    72	square-root choices.  The formal helper therefore separates the prefactor and
    73	exponent.\footnote{The helper is \leanid{IsPolyErr} in

    51	\begin{definition}
    52	Given integer $d,m$ and a prime power $q$ we denote by $\ideg_{d,m}(\F_q)$ the set of polynomials in $m$ variables
    53	  with \emph{individual} degree at most $d$ in each variable. When the field is clear from context we write $\ideg_{d,m}$. 	
    54		When
    55	  the number of variables is clear from context we
    56	  write $\ideg_d$. We denote by $\deg_{d}$ the set of polynomials with
    57	  \emph{total} degree at most $d$.

    60	Recall the low-degree code defined in \Cref{sec:ld-encoding}, in which vectors $h \in \F_q^\nqubits$ get mapped to polynomials $g_h \in \ideg_{d,m}(\F_q)$ such that for every $u \in \{0,1\}^m$, $g_h(u) = h_u$ where the coordinates of $h$ are indexed by binary strings of length $m$. For $x\in \F_q^m$, recall the definition of the vector $\ind_m(x) \in \F_q^\nqubits$ from Section~\ref{sec:ld-encoding}. Recall also the finite field trace $\tr(\cdot)=\tr_{q\to 2}(\cdot):\F_q\to\F_2$, where $q=2^k$ for odd $k$, defined in Section~\ref{sec:subfields}. 
    61	
    62	
    63	
    64	Call a tuple $\omega = (u_\xpt,u_\zpt,r_\xpt,r_\zpt) \in (\F_q^m)^2
    65	\times (\F_q)^2$ \emph{anticommuting} if the quantity 
    66	 \[\gamma\,=\,\tr ((r_\xpt \cdot
    67	\ind_m(u_\xpt)) \cdot (r_\zpt \cdot \ind_m(u_\zpt)))\]
    68	introduced in~\Cref{eq:gamma-value} is not $0$, and \emph{commuting} if $\gamma=0$.
    69	
    70	\begin{fact}
    71	\label{fact:omega-anticomm-prob}
    72		The probability that a tuple $\omega= (u_\xpt,u_\zpt,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)$ sampled uniformly at random from $(\F_q^m)^2 \times (\F_q)^2$
    73		is anti-commuting is at least 
    74		\[
    75			(1 - q^{-m}) \cdot (1 - q^{-1}) \cdot \Big (1 - \frac{md}{q} \Big )  \cdot \frac{1}{2} \geq \Big (1 - \frac{3md}{q} \Big ) \cdot \frac{1}{2}.
    76		\]
    77		The probability that $\omega$ is commuting is also at least $\Big(1 - \frac{3md}{q} \Big ) \cdot \frac{1}{2}$.
    78	\end{fact}
    79	\begin{proof}
    80		First, note that $\ind_m(u_\xpt) = 0$ if and only if $u_\xpt = 0$. If $u_\xpt=0$ then $\omega$ is commuting. Otherwise, if $u_\xpt \neq 0$, then observe that for all $r_\xpt, r_\zpt, u_\zpt$,
    81		\begin{align*}
    82			\tr( (r_\xpt \cdot \ind_m(u_\xpt)) \cdot (r_\zpt \cdot
    83	                \ind_m(u_\zpt))) &= \tr( r_\xpt r_\zpt (\ind_m(u_\xpt) \cdot \ind_m(u_\zpt))) \\
    84									&= \tr( (r_\xpt r_\zpt) \cdot g_{\ind_m(u_\xpt)}(u_\zpt))\;,
    85		\end{align*}
    86		where $g_{\ind_m(u_\xpt)}$ is a nonzero polynomial in $\ideg_{d,m}(\F_q)$.
    87		
    88		If $r_\xpt = 0$, then $\omega$ is commuting. Condition on $r_\xpt \neq 0$.  Since $g_{\ind_m(u_\xpt)}\neq 0$ has total degree at most $md$, by the Schwartz-Zippel lemma the probability that $g_{\ind_m(u_\xpt)}(u_\zpt)$ is zero over a uniformly random choice of $u_\zpt$ is at most $md/q$. Conditioned on $g_{\ind_m(u_\xpt)}(u_\zpt) \neq 0$, the product $(r_\xpt r_\zpt) \cdot g_{\ind_m(u_\xpt)}(u_\zpt)$ is a uniformly random element of $\F_q$ when $r_\zpt$ is chosen uniformly at random. 
    89		
    90		The probability that $u_\xpt \neq 0, r_\xpt \neq 0, g_{\ind_m(u_\xpt)}(u_\zpt) \neq 0$ is at least $(1 - q^{-m}) \cdot (1 - q^{-1}) \cdot (1 - md/q)$ since $u_\xpt, r_\xpt, u_\zpt$ are chosen independently.
    91		
    92		Since $q = 2^t$ is an admissible field size, we have that for all $a \in \F_q$, the trace of $a$ is equal to $\sum_i a_i$ where $(a_1,\ldots,a_t)=\kappa(a) \in \F_2^t$ are defined in Section~\ref{sec:subfields}. Thus the probability that a uniformly random element of $\F_q$ has trace $0$ is exactly $1/2$. 
    93	\end{proof}

    95	In this appendix we often use the ``$\approx_\delta$'' notation to specify closeness of general operators (not necessarily POVMs) that are indexed by questions but not answers: given sets of operators $\{A^x \}$ and $\{B^x\}$ indexed by questions $x \in \cal{X}$, we write $A^x \approx_\delta B^x$ to denote \[
    96		\E_{x \sim \mu} \bra{\psi} (A^x - B^x)^\dagger (A^x - B^x)
    97	        \ket{\psi}\,\leq\, O(\delta)
    98	      \]
    99	where $\mu$ is a question distribution and $\ket{\psi}$ is a state that has been fixed by context. This will be useful for expressing closeness of observables, for example. The following two lemmas relate the closeness between sets of operators and weighted sums of those operators. 
   100	\begin{lemma}
   101	\label{lem:avg-closeness}
   102	Let $\{A^x \}$ and $\{B^x\}$ be operators indexed by some finite set $\mathcal{X}$, and let $\mu$ be a probability distribution over $\mathcal{X}$. Let $\{\alpha_x \}$ be a set of complex numbers such that $|\alpha_x| \leq 1$. Then if $A^x \approx_\delta B^x$ on average over $x$ drawn from $\mu$, then $A \approx_\delta B$, where $A = \E_x \alpha_x A^x$ and $B= \E_x \alpha_x B^x$.
   103	\end{lemma}
   104	\begin{proof}
   105	Expand
   106	\begin{align*}
   107		\Big\| \E_x \alpha_x \big ( A^x - B^x \big) \ket{\psi} \Big\|^2 &\leq \Big( \E_x \norm{ (A^x -B^x) \ket{\psi}} \Big)^2 \\
   108		&\leq \E_x \norm{(A^x - B^x) \ket{\psi}}^2 \\
   109		&\leq \delta\;.
   110	\end{align*}
   111	The first inequality is the triangle inequality and the second inequality is Jensen's inequality. 
   112	\end{proof}

   114	\begin{lemma}
   115	\label{lem:povm-to-obs}
   116	Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a finite set. Let $\{A^x_a \}_{a \in \mathcal{A}}$ and $\{B^x_a\}_{a \in \mathcal{A}}$ be POVMs and let $\{ \alpha_a \}_{a \in \mathcal{A}}$ be a collection of complex numbers on the unit circle. Let $A^x = \sum_a \alpha_a A^x_a$ and $B^x = \sum_a  \alpha_a B^x_a$. Then 
   117	\[
   118		A^x_a \approx_\delta B^x_a \quad \text{implies} \quad A^x \approx_{\delta'} B^x
   119	\]
   120	for $\delta' = |\mathcal{A}| \cdot \delta$.
   121	\end{lemma}
   122	\begin{proof}
   123	Expand
   124		\begin{align*}
   125			\E_x \norm{(A^x - B^x) \ket{\psi}}^2 &= \E_x \Big\|\sum_a \alpha_a (A^x_a - B^x_a) \ket{\psi}\Big\|^2 \\
   126			&\leq \E_x \Big( \sum_a \norm{ (A^x_a - B^x_a) \ket{\psi}} \Big)^2 \\
   127			&\leq \E_x |\mathcal{A}| \cdot \sum_a \norm{ (A^x_a - B^x_a) \ket{\psi}}^2 \\
   128			&\leq |\mathcal{A}| \cdot \delta\;.
   129		\end{align*}
   130	The first inequality follows from the triangle inequality, the second inequality follows from Cauchy-Schwarz, and the last inequality follows from the assumption that $A^x_a \approx_\delta B^x_a$. 
   131	\end{proof}

Let $\ket{\psi}$ be a state on $\mH_\alice \otimes \mH_\bob$ where $\mH_\alice,\mH_\bob$ are finite dimensional.    367	\paragraph{Expanded state.} We introduce registers $\alice', \alice'', \bob', \bob''$ that are each isomorphic to $(\C^q)^{\otimes \nqubits}$. Define the state \begin{equation}\label{eq:def-psihat}
   368		\ket{\hat{\psi}}_{\alice \alice' \alice'' \bob \bob' \bob''} = (\ket{\psi})_{\alice \bob} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}_{\alice' \alice''} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}_{\bob' \bob''}\;,
   369	\end{equation}
   370	where we have added maximally entangled states in registers
   371	$\alice' \alice''$ and $\bob' \bob''$; recall also that the state $\ket{\psi}$ is already implicitly  appended with sufficiently many ancilla qubits initialized in the $\ket{0}$ state. 
   372	For the remainder of the Appendix all approximations will be evaluated with respect to this state.
   373	
   374	\paragraph{Expanded observables.} For all $W \in \{X,Z\}$, $r \in \F_q$, and $u \in \F_q^m$ define the following observable $\hat{W}^r(u)$: \begin{equation}\label{eq:lc-23}
   375		\hat{W}^r(u) = W^r(u) \otimes \tau^W(r \cdot \ind_m(u))\;,
   376	\end{equation}
   377	where $W^r(u)$ is the observable defined in \Cref{eq:qld-strat-obs} and $\tau^W(r \cdot \ind_m(u))$ is the generalized Pauli observable (see \Cref{sec:generalized-pauli}) acting on $(\C^q)^{\otimes \nqubits}$. 
   378	
   379	For $a\in \F_q$ define corresponding projections
   380	\[
   381		\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_a = \E_{r \in \F_q} (-1)^{\tr(ar)} \, \hat{W}^r(u)\;.
   382	\]
   383	Note that $\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_a$ can be equivalently
   384	written as a sum of projectors by applying Fourier
   385	identities. Specifically, for $W \in \{X, Z\}$, $u \in \F_q^{m}$, and
   386	$a \in \F_q$, define the projector
   387	\begin{equation} \tau^{W, u}_{a} =
   388	  \tau^{W}_{[ g_{\cdot}(u) = a]} = \sum_{h \in \F_q^{\nqubits}: h
   389	    \cdot \ind_m(u) = a} \tau^{W}_{h}\;. \label{eq:qld-point-obs-def} \end{equation}
   390	Then we can write $\hat{M}^{(\Point, W), u}_a$ as follows:
   391	\begin{align*}
   392	  \hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_a
   393	  &= \E_{r \in \F_q} (-1)^{\tr(ar)} \,
   394	    W^r(u) \otimes \tau^W(r
   395	    \cdot \ind_m(u)) \\
   396	    &= \E_{r \in \F_q}
   397	    (-1)^{\tr(ar)} \, \Big(\sum_{a' \in \F_q}(-1)^{\tr (a' r)} M^{(\Point,W),u}_{a'}
   398	    \Big) \otimes \Big(
   399	    \sum_{h \in \F_q^n}
   400	    (-1)^{\tr( r( h \cdot \ind_m(u)))} \tau^{W}_{h} \Big) \\
   401	  &= \E_{r \in \F_q}
   402	    (-1)^{\tr(ar)} \, \Big(\sum_{a' \in \F_q}(-1)^{\tr (a' r)} M^{(\Point,W),u}_{a'}
   403	    \Big) \otimes \Big(
   404	    \sum_{a'' \in \F_q}
   405	    (-1)^{\tr(a'' r)} \tau^{W,u}_{a''} \Big) \\
   406	  &=	\sum_{a',a'' \in \F_q} \E_{r \in \F_q} (-1)^{\tr((a + a' + a'')r)} \, M^{(\Point,W),u}_{a'}  \otimes \tau^{W,u}_{a''} \\
   407	  &= \sum_{\substack{a',a'' \in \F_q \\ a' + a'' = a}}  \, M^{(\Point,W),u}_{a'}  \otimes \tau^{W,u}_{a''}\;,
   408	\end{align*}
   409	where in the second line we have used \Cref{eq:qld-strat-obs} on the
   410	first tensor factor and \Cref{eq:pauli-obs-proj} on the second, and in the third line we
   411	have used \Cref{eq:qld-point-obs-def}.
   412	For a fixed $u\in\F_q^m$, $r \in \F_q$ and $b \in \F_2$, define a projection
   413	\begin{equation}
   414		\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u,r}_b = \sum_{a \in \F_q : \tr(ar) = b}
   415	        \hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_a\;, \label{eq:qld-def-mptur}
   416	\end{equation}
   417	which can be equivalently written as
   418	\begin{equation}\label{eq:lc-22}
   419	\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u,r}_b = \frac{1}{2} \Big ( \Id + (-1)^b \hat{W}^r(u) \Big)\;.
   420	\end{equation}

   422	The registers that the operators $\hat{W}^r(u)$,
   423	$\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_a$, and $\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u,r}_b$ act on
   424	depend on context. For example if $W^r(u)$ is viewed as an operator
   425	acting on register $\alice$, then we will view $\hat{W}^r(u)$ as
   426	acting on registers $\alice \alice'$ (with the $\tau^W$ observable
   427	acting on register $\alice'$). We generally indicate via subscripts
   428	which registers the operators act on (for example we will write
   429	$(\hat{W}^r(u))_{\alice \alice'}$ or $(\hat{W}^r(u))_{\bob

   433	
   434	\paragraph{Partitioning the registers, and symmetries}
   435	In the remainder of this section as well as \Cref{sec:combining,sec:apply-ldt}, we will partition the six registers
   436	$\alice \alice' \alice'' \bob \bob' \bob''$ into
   437	two ``parties'' in two different ways. The first is to consider
   438	$\alice \alice'$ together to form  a single party, and $\bob \alice''$
   439	to form the second party. The second is to consider $\bob \bob'$ to
   440	form the first party, and $\alice \bob''$ to form the second
   441	party. Thanks to the symmetry of the Pauli basis test under exchanging the
   442	two players, as well as the symmetry of the ancilla states in
   443	registers $\alice' \alice''$ and $\bob' \bob''$, every ``bipartite'' consistency relation we derive between two
   444	operators $M, N$ will hold for both of the two bipartitioning schemes,
   445	and with the first and second party interchanged. That is, whenever we

1	# Mathematical Language Guidelines
     2	
     3	MIPStarRE Lean names and documentation should be written for readers comparing
     4	the formalization with the paper and blueprint.
     5	
     6	This is a project-local supplement to the Mathlib-derived documentation,
     7	naming, and style guides in the lean-conventions skill's `MATHLIB_doc`,
     8	`MATHLIB_naming`, and `MATHLIB_style` references.
     9	
    10	## Scope
    11	
    12	These guidelines apply to:
    13	
    14	- public Lean declaration names and namespace names;
    15	- module docstrings;
    16	- declaration docstrings;
    17	- documentation-visible section comments;
    18	- explanatory comments that describe the mathematical role of a declaration.
    19	- blueprint prose and formalization-support notes;
    20	- issue titles and issue bodies;
    21	- PR titles and PR descriptions.
    22	
    23	## Source of Truth
    24	
    25	Use terminology from the following sources, in this order:
    26	
    27	1. `references/ldt-paper/`
    28	2. `blueprint/src/chapter/`
    29	3. established local conventions in nearby Lean files
    30	
    31	When the paper has a term for the object, use that term. For Section 5, for
    32	example, prefer orthogonalization lemma, truncation function, rounding to
    33	projectors, rank reduction, and completing to measurement.
    34	
    35	## Reference Notation And Terminology
    36	
    37	The notation and terminology of the original reference are the default for
    38	reader-facing mathematical text.  A reader should be able to compare a Lean
    39	docstring, blueprint paragraph, issue, or PR description with the cited source
    40	without first learning a private vocabulary used by the formalization.
    41	
    42	When Lean must use a different name or representation, define the deviation in a
    43	location which future readers can find from the affected statement.  Use the
    44	first applicable location in the following order:
    45	
    46	1. the declaration docstring of the public object whose name or representation
    47	   differs from the paper;
    48	2. the module docstring of the defining Lean file, when the deviation concerns a
    49	   family of declarations in that file;
    50	3. the relevant blueprint paragraph, when the notation appears only in the
    51	   blueprint;
    52	4. a report under `docs/reports/` or `docs/paper-gaps/`, when the deviation is a
    53	   larger discrepancy between the paper, blueprint, and Lean.
    54	
    55	The explanation should say:
    56	
    57	- the notation or term used in the paper;
    58	- the Lean object or name which represents it;
    59	- the mathematical reason for the difference, if there is one;
    60	- the scope in which the replacement should be used.
    61	
    62	A PR description may mention the deviation, but it should not be the only place
    63	where future readers can learn it.
    64	
    65	Formalization-only auxiliary lemmas should be introduced as such.  Their prose
    66	should name the nearby paper equation, theorem, or construction they support,
    67	rather than presenting the auxiliary name as paper terminology.
    68	
    69	## Naming Norm
    70	
    71	Names and prose should describe the mathematical object, hypothesis, or
    72	conclusion. They should not encode the history of how the formalization was
    73	assembled.
    74	
    75	Avoid presenting words such as `pipeline`, `wrapper`, `package`, `raw`,
    76	`oneShot`, or `liveBlock` as mathematical terminology unless the cited source
    77	uses them with that meaning. Likewise, avoid implementation-local substitutes
    78	such as `projectivization` or `spectral truncation` when the paper gives a
    79	clearer phrase.
    80	
    81	This is a general rule for the repository, not only a rule for file splits.
    82	Module names, namespace names, public declarations, theorem fields, docstrings,
    83	blueprint-facing names, issue titles, and spec documents should name the
    84	mathematical layer under discussion, not the local workflow step, paper line
    85	number, or implementation history.
    86	
    87	### Concrete examples
    88	
    89	The table below illustrates the naming norm with examples patterned on the
    90	codebase and on names seen during review.  Some entries are existing names;
    91	others are proposed names for future refactors.  The "avoid" column lists
    92	process-shaped names that encode the history of how the formalization was
    93	assembled; the "prefer" column lists mathematical names that a reader of the
    94	paper or blueprint would recognize.
    95	
    96	| Avoid (process-shaped)                        | Prefer (mathematical)                     | Rationale                                              |
    97	|:----------------------------------------------|:------------------------------------------|:-------------------------------------------------------|
    98	| `Line130`                                     | `ProjectiveConsistency`                   | Paper Lemma 5.13, not "the line-130 identity"          |
    99	| `Line169`                                     | `CompletionTransport`                     | Paper Lemma 5.16, step that transports completed data  |
   100	| `Step6`                                       | `Orthonormalization`                      | Paper Section 5, the orthonormalization construction   |
   101	| `FinalAssembly`                               | `DiagonalCompletion`                      | Paper Lemma 5.17, constructing a diagonal POVM         |
   102	| `OneShotIneq`                                 | `SelfConsistencyDataProcessing` (or existing module `Preliminaries.SelfConsistency.DataProcessing`)           | Paper's data-processing inequality for self-consistency |
   103	| `PipelineCheck`                               | `ErrorPropagationBound` (proposed)                   | The bound that propagates error through the test       |
   104	| `QxpLayerWrapper`                             | `ProjectivePOVMCompletion` (proposed)                | The construction from round-projectors to POVMs        |
   105	| `RawSpectralTruncation`                       | `SpectralTruncation`                      | The paper's spectral truncation, not an "unwrapped" version |
   106	| `AddInUStep3To5`                              | `AddInUUpperExcessMass` (proposed)                  | Paper Addendum in §U, the upper excess-mass estimate   |
   107	| `AddInUStep12`                                | `AddInUCommutationTail` (proposed)                   | Paper Addendum in §U, the commutation tail estimate    |
   108	
   109	An avoided name is acceptable only when the cited paper itself uses that
   110	phrase as the mathematical name (e.g., a lemma the paper calls "Step 2").
   111	In that case the docstring should cite the paper's phrasing.
   112	
   113	File-split PRs are a common place where this rule matters: new leaves should be
   114	named by the mathematical boundary they isolate, and any public declarations
   115	exposed by the split should be reviewed under the same standard.
   116	
   117	### Shared helpers
   118	
   119	When the same (or nearly the same) helper declaration appears in two or
   120	more chapter-local leaves, the copies should be consolidated into a single
   121	shared helper in an appropriate common module.  This avoids duplication and
   122	ensures that fixes, generalizations, or upstream replacements apply to all
   123	call sites at once.  Issue [#1145] tracks this work across the repository.
   124	
   125	Procedure:
   126	
   127	1. **Confirm equivalence.**  Compare the statement of each copy.  If the
   128	   types differ only by a chapter-specific parameterization (e.g.,
   129	   `SubMeas (Polynomial params) ι` vs `SubMeas (Point params) ι`),
   130	   parameterize the shared helper over that type via a `variable` or
   131	   explicit argument.
   132	2. **Find the right home.**  Prefer a module that is already imported by
   133	   both call sites.  Typical candidates:
   134	   - `MIPStarRE/LDT/Basic/` for parameter-free operators and bounds,
   135	   - `MIPStarRE/LDT/Preliminaries/` for polynomial/field/character lemmas,
   136	   - The highest chapter that is a common dependency of the two sites.
   137	3. **Name mathematically.**  Give the shared helper a name that describes
   138	   what it states, not which chapter it originally came from.
   139	4. **Replace call sites.**  Delete the chapter-local copies and replace
   140	   their uses with the shared helper.  A thin wrapper is allowed only when it
   141	   preserves a paper-facing or blueprint-facing name that external readers
   142	   need to search for; such wrappers should have a docstring or compatibility
   143	   comment explaining why the alias exists.  Remove the wrapper once that
   144	   paper-facing name is no longer needed for external reference.
   145	5. **Document.**  Add a docstring to the shared helper citing the paper or
   146	   blueprint location it supports.
   147	
   148	### Legacy identifier treatment
   149	
   150	If a docstring must mention a legacy Lean identifier, cite it in backticks and
   151	describe the mathematical object in paper terminology. If an old public
   152	identifier cannot be renamed in the current PR, record the required migration
   153	in the issue, PR description, or an audit file under `audits/`.
   154	
   155	Do not add an empty pass-through abbreviation merely to introduce a second
   156	public name.  This is different from a documented public wrapper allowed in the
   157	shared-helper procedure above: a wrapper must preserve a paper-facing or
   158	blueprint-facing term and must say why the alias exists.
   159	
   160	## Review Checklist
   161	
   162	Reviewers should use this checklist when examining public names and
   163	documentation prose.  Flag any item that fails.
   164	
   165	- [ ] **Naming.**  Do public declaration names, namespace names, module names,
   166	      theorem field names, and docstring prose describe a mathematical object,
   167	      hypothesis, or conclusion?  Or do they encode the history of how the
   168	      formalization was assembled (paper line numbers, workflow steps,
   169	      implementation-phase labels)?
   170	- [ ] **Source alignment.**  For the mathematical content under review, does
   171	      the prose use the terminology in `references/ldt-paper/` or the
   172	      blueprint?  Are process words such as `pipeline`, `wrapper`, `package`,
   173	      `raw`, `oneShot`, or `liveBlock` used as mathematical terms when the
   174	      source does not use them that way?
   175	- [ ] **Deviation documented.**  If a Lean name or representation differs from
   176	      the paper, is the deviation documented in a declaration docstring,
   177	      module docstring, blueprint paragraph, or `docs/paper-gaps/` note, in
   178	      that order of preference?
   179	- [ ] **Auxiliary lemmas.**  Are formalization-only auxiliary lemmas introduced
   180	      as such, with prose naming the nearby paper equation, theorem, or
   181	      construction they support?
   182	- [ ] **Shared helpers.**  Does the PR introduce a helper that already exists
   183	      (or near-exists) in another chapter-local leaf?  If so, has it been
   184	      consolidated into a common module with a mathematical name?
   185	- [ ] **Legacy IDs.**  If a legacy Lean identifier is mentioned, is the
   186	      mathematical object described in paper terminology?  If an old public
   187	      identifier cannot be renamed yet, is the required migration recorded in
   188	      the issue, PR description, or an audit file?
   189	- [ ] **Pass-through names.**  Does the PR add an empty pass-through
   190	      abbreviation that introduces a second public name without adding
   191	      mathematical content?  Reject it unless it is a documented compatibility
   192	      wrapper preserving paper-facing or blueprint-facing terminology.
   193	
   194	Review-fix PRs touching a surface covered by an active audit should read the
   195	relevant audit before changing names or prose.

+/-!
+# Typed strategy measurements and point observables
+
+This file fixes a projective, possibly heterogeneous strategy for the Pauli
+basis test and extracts the typed measurement families used in the analysis.
+Malformed answers are folded into a fixed valid answer, so the extracted
+families remain complete measurements. Their original wrong-form mass is kept
+separately and bounded by named proof obligations. `Option` is used only for
+the completed line-evaluation classes.
+
+## References
+
+The ambient strategy convention and the observable `W^r(u)` are in
+`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:160-190`,
+corresponding to `def:strategy-observables` in
+`blueprint/src/chapter/ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:480-503`. The typed question
+and answer forms come from `def:pauli-question-distribution` and
+`def:pauli-win-predicate`, paper
+`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1225`
+and blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:310-392`.
+-/
+
+open scoped BigOperators Matrix ComplexOrder
+
+namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
+
+open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.Quantum
+
+noncomputable section
+
+/-- The two local registers of a heterogeneous bipartite strategy. This is
+formalization-only indexing for the player-dependent notation at paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:160-190`. -/
+inductive PlayerSide where
+  | alice
+  | bob
+  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited, Fintype
+
+/-- A projective strategy satisfying the winning premise used throughout
+Section `sec:commutation`. The structure retains the distinct player spaces and
+measurement families of `Strategy`. Paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:160-172`; blueprint
+`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:385-475`. -/
+structure ProjectiveSetting (P : AdmissibleParams) (ε : ℝ) where
+  toStrategy : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P)
+  isProjective : toStrategy.IsProjective
+  win : 1 - ε ≤ toStrategy.value
+
+namespace ProjectiveSetting
+
+variable {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε : ℝ}
+
+/-- The local Hilbert-space index type on a specified player side. This is the
+dependent carrier behind the side-qualified operators at paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:174-190`. -/
+def LocalSpace (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) : PlayerSide → Type
+  | .alice => S.toStrategy.ιA
+  | .bob => S.toStrategy.ιB
+
+instance localSpaceFintype (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide) :
+    Fintype (S.LocalSpace side) := by
+  cases side <;> simp only [LocalSpace] <;> infer_instance
+
+instance localSpaceDecidableEq (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide) :
+    DecidableEq (S.LocalSpace side) := by
+  cases side <;> simp only [LocalSpace] <;> infer_instance
+
+/-- Select the strategy measurement before outcome postprocessing on one
+player side. This is the heterogeneous interpretation of the shared symbol `M` at
+paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:160-184`. -/
+def rawMeasurement (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
+    (question : PauliQuestion P) :
+    Measurement (PauliAnswer P) (S.LocalSpace side) := by
+  cases side with
+  | alice => exact S.toStrategy.A question
+  | bob => exact S.toStrategy.B question
+
+/-- Embed a point into the full Pauli question space in basis `W`. This is the
+point-question content from `def:pauli-question-distribution`, paper
+`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:997-1008`, blueprint
+`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:310-354`. -/
+def contentOfPoint (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
+    (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) : PauliSpace P :=
+  embedLd P W fun i =>
+    match i with
+    | .inl (.inl j) => u j
+    | .inl (.inr _) => 0
+    | .inr _ => 0
+
+/-- Embed a canonical line description into the full Pauli question space.
+Axis lines clear the direction block, whereas diagonal lines retain their
+canonical projected direction. Paper
+`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:997-1008`; blueprint
+`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:310-354` and `rem:deg-line-representatives`. -/
+def contentOfLine (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
+    (line : LineDesc P.toLdParams) : PauliSpace P :=
+  embedLd P W fun i =>
+    match i with
+    | .inl (.inl j) => line.base j
+    | .inl (.inr _) => line.seed
+    | .inr j =>
+        match line with
+        | .axis _ _ _ => 0
+        | .diagonal _ _ direction _ _ => direction j
+
+/-- Fill the point, scalar, and phase blocks shared by Pair, Pair/W, and Magic
+Square questions. This is the type-4 content of
+`def:pauli-question-distribution`, paper
+`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1030-1120`, blueprint
+`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:310-354`. -/
+def contentOfTuple (P : AdmissibleParams)
+    (uX uZ : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) (rX rZ : PauliScalar P) : PauliSpace P :=
+  fun i =>
+    match i with
+    | .inl (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inl j)))) => uX j
+    | .inl (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inr j)))) => uZ j
+    | .inl (.inl (.inl (.inr _))) => 0
+    | .inl (.inl (.inr _)) => 0
+    | .inl (.inr _) => rX
+    | .inr _ => rZ
+
+/-- The typed point question in basis `W`, from the strategy notation at paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:174-190` and
+`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:310-354`. -/
+def pointQuestion (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
+    (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) : PauliQuestion P :=
+  (.point W, contentOfPoint P W u)
+
+/-- The typed axis or diagonal line question represented by a canonical
+`LineDesc`. Paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:174-184`; blueprint
+`def:strategy-observables` and `rem:deg-line-representatives`. -/
+def lineQuestion (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
+    (line : LineDesc P.toLdParams) : PauliQuestion P :=
+  match line.kind with
+  | .axis => (.aline W, contentOfLine P W line)
+  | .diagonal => (.dline W, contentOfLine P W line)
+
+/-- The typed Pair question for a tuple `(u_X,u_Z,r_X,r_Z)`. Paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:210-249`; blueprint
+`lem:qld-win-implications`. -/
+def pairQuestion (P : AdmissibleParams)
+    (uX uZ : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) (rX rZ : PauliScalar P) : PauliQuestion P :=
+  (.pair, contentOfTuple P uX uZ rX rZ)
+
+/-- The typed Pair/W question for a tuple `(u_X,u_Z,r_X,r_Z)`. Paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:210-249`; blueprint
+`lem:qld-win-implications`. -/
+def pairWQuestion (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
+    (uX uZ : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) (rX rZ : PauliScalar P) : PauliQuestion P :=
+  (.pairW W, contentOfTuple P uX uZ rX rZ)
+
+/-- The typed Magic Square question for a tuple `(u_X,u_Z,r_X,r_Z)`. Paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:213-258`; blueprint
+`lem:qld-win-implications`. -/
+def msQuestion (P : AdmissibleParams) (t : MsType)
+    (uX uZ : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) (rX rZ : PauliScalar P) : PauliQuestion P :=
+  (.ms t, contentOfTuple P uX uZ rX rZ)
+
+/-- A typed question occurs in the Pauli-test distribution when it appears on
+at least one side of a supported question pair. This Lean-only predicate makes
+the support guarantees for the question embeddings precise; blueprint
+`def:pauli-question-distribution`, `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:310-354`, paper
+`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`. -/
+def QuestionAppearsInSupport (P : AdmissibleParams) (question : PauliQuestion P) : Prop :=
+  ∃ other : PauliQuestion P,
+    (question, other) ∈ (pauliQuestionDistribution P).support ∨
+      (other, question) ∈ (pauliQuestionDistribution P).support
+
+/-- Point embeddings occur in the typed Pauli question support. This is the
+support well-formedness companion to `def:pauli-question-distribution`,
+blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:310-354`, paper
+`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:997-1008`. -/
+theorem pointQuestion_appears_in_support (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
+    (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :
+    QuestionAppearsInSupport P (pointQuestion P W u) := by
+  sorry
+
+/-- Canonical axis and diagonal line embeddings occur in the typed Pauli
+question support. This is the line companion to
+`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:310-354`,
+paper `08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:997-1008`. -/
+theorem lineQuestion_appears_in_support (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
+    (line : LineDesc P.toLdParams) :
+    QuestionAppearsInSupport P (lineQuestion P W line) := by
+  sorry
+
+/-- Pair embeddings occur in the typed Pauli question support. This is the
+Pair companion to `def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint
+`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:310-354`, paper
+`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1030-1057`. -/
+theorem pairQuestion_appears_in_support (P : AdmissibleParams)
+    (uX uZ : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) (rX rZ : PauliScalar P) :
+    QuestionAppearsInSupport P (pairQuestion P uX uZ rX rZ) := by
+  sorry
+
+/-- Pair/W embeddings occur in the typed Pauli question support. This is the
+Pair/W companion to `def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint
+`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:310-354`, paper
+`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1030-1057`. -/
+theorem pairWQuestion_appears_in_support (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
+    (uX uZ : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) (rX rZ : PauliScalar P) :
+    QuestionAppearsInSupport P (pairWQuestion P W uX uZ rX rZ) := by
+  sorry
+
+/-- Magic Square embeddings occur in the typed Pauli question support. This is
+the Magic Square companion to `def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint
+`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:310-354`, paper
+`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1059-1120`. -/

    36	/-- Source-style left/right relation `A^x_a ⊗ I ≈_δ I ⊗ B^x_a`. -/
    37	structure BipartiteSDDRel {Question Outcome : Type*} {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]

    39	    (ψ : QuantumState (ι × ι)) (𝒟 : Distribution Question)

item.text: The late comparison exposes one new regression from the previous repair: item 2 now has the common square-root bound in Lean, but the blueprint still separately advertises the stronger \(O(\varepsilon)\) refinement. I’ve also confirmed that the sole `\notready` remains appropriate; the unresolved status defects are all overclaimed statement-level `\leanok` blocks, not proof-level tags.

## Findings

- [ ] F1 (blocker) `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/Defs.lean:287` — Fixed-outcome folding changes the source point measurement and therefore the observable certified by `\leanok`.
- [ ] F2 (changes) `blueprint/src/chapter/ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:87` — The polynomial-class `\leanok` overclaims projectivity preservation and a zero bottom class.

- [ ] F8 (changes) `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/ExpandedDefs.lean:137` — `expObs` lacks the Hermitian/involution property asserted for the expanded observable.
- [ ] F9 (changes) `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/ExpandedDefs.lean:157` — `tauPointProj` lacks the projector or projective-family property asserted by the blueprint.

## Review

F1 is the principal mathematical blocker. The blueprint defines \(W^r(u)\) from the strategy effects \(M_a^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}\) at lines 524–530. Lean’s `pointAnswerOrZero` and `pointMeas` instead add every wrong-form effect to outcome zero, after which `pointObs` uses that altered effect. The wrong-form mass bounds do not establish equality with the source measurement. The source-facing `\leanok` must wait for an actual strategy-replacement reduction or a faithful question-specific measurement.

F2–F7 are early status mismatches. `evalOpt` only defines an outcome relabeling; it proves neither projectivity preservation nor the zero `none` fiber asserted at blueprint lines 87–90. `AdmissibleParams` adds \(d\ge1\) and \(m\mid q\) to the broader preliminary parameter scope. There is no theorem `commProb = 1 - anticommProb`. `opDistSq` does not include the universal-constant comparison defining \(\approx_\delta\). Finally, the generalized statements in F6 and F7 imply source cases but do not have the exact source quantifiers required for these tags; source-shaped corollaries should carry the `\leanok`.

F8–F10 and F12 concern properties asserted but not represented in signatures. Add direct Hermitian/involution, projector, and projective-family declarations as appropriate. These derived facts should also be split from the surrounding `definition` environments into lemma or theorem entries.

For F11, the independent prefactor and exponent in `IsPolyErr` are a justified local correction, documented in `qpbt_polynomial-error-square-root.tex`. The two blueprint statements at lines 1056 and 1173 must explicitly state and cite that corrected convention before their `\leanok` tags are accurate.

F13 arose alongside the successful common-error repair: `expLine_point_cons` now uses `deltaLine ε = sqrt ε`, but the blueprint still advertises the stronger \(O(\varepsilon)\) refinement. Either formalize that refinement or remove it from the certified statement. For F14, either state the documented \(\mathbb F_q\cup\{\bot\}\) correction in item 3 or provide a separate theorem restricted to field outcomes.

The prose repairs are direct: rename `rawMeasurement` to `strategyMeasurement`, rename `junkMass` and its theorems to `wrongFormMass`, replace F17 with “the winning hypothesis bounds the resulting wrong-form mass by the rejection probability,” replace F18 with “local Hilbert-space index set,” and describe F19 as recording which player’s local Hilbert space occurs in each placement.

The current head does fix the earlier consistency endpoint, state normalization, common-error, factor-interchange, total-degree, placement-enumeration, and most prose findings. The sole `\notready` at blueprint line 946 remains appropriate.
